findings.finding: Use f(S)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=S. For odd S, choose a=x,b=2x,c=2xk (k≥2) ⇒ S=x(3+2k). Then t=LCM=2x=2S/d where d=3+2k odd divisor≥7. Minimum t≥6S/11; equality when 11|S using t, t/2, t/3. Since M=3^{L}, L=2025! divisible by 11, all N_i≡0 (mod 11). Thus f(N_i)=6N_i/11. Compute A_i=⌊L·f(N_i)/M⌋=⌊(6L/11)·(N_i/M)⌋. For c small, N_i/M≈1 ⇒ A_i=6L/11. For c=4M, N_i/M=5 ⇒ A_i=30L/11. Sum A=5·6L/11+30L/11=60L/11 ⇒ Σg= (60L/11)/L=60/11. Reduced p/q=60/11 ⇒ p+q=71. Answer: 71.

Key: f(N)=min c with proper divisors a,b of c, a+b=N−c. Lower bound c≥⌈6N/11⌉; equality iff N≡0 (mod 11) → f(N)=6N/11. Otherwise use odd divisor d≥7: set a=x, b=2x, c=2x·k ⇒ N=x(3+2k), c=2xk=2N/(3+2k). So f(N)=min_{odd d|N,d≥7}2N/d. Compute M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod 11). For each N_i=M+c_i, find largest odd divisor d_i (≥7). Then f(N_i)=2N_i/d_i. Compute g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025!. Since 2025! divisible by 11, floor simplifies to (6·2025!/11)*(N_i/M) for N_i≡0 (mod 11) else (2·2025!/d_i)*(N_i/M). Sum yields 60/11 → p+q=71. (Check mod 11 residues, d_i values).

We need f(N)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N. Write a=N/p, b=N/q, c=N/r where p,q,r>1, distinct, and N·pq/(pq+p+q)=c integer. Minimal ratio r= pq/(pq+p+q) occurs for (p,q) giving smallest r with (D/g)│N, where D=pq+p+q, g=gcd(pq,D). For each N_i=M+c, M=3^L (L=2025!), M≡1 (mod d) for any odd d≤2025, d∤3. So N_i≡1+c (mod d). Check small d (11,7,5,13,17,…) dividing 1+c_i. Choose smallest r: (2,3)→r=6/11 if 11│N; else (2,4)→r=4/7 if 7│N; else (2,6)→r=3/5 if 5│N; else larger. Compute K_i=L·r (integer since D|L). Then A_i=K_i (small c) or 5K_i (for N=5M). Sum A_i=60L/11 ⇒ sum g=60/11 ⇒ p+q=71 ⇒ answer 71.

f(N)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N. Ratio r=LCM/N= (pq)/(pq+p+q). D/g= (pq+p+q)/g must divide N. For N=M (3^L) only d=3 works →r=2/3. For N=5M, d=5 works →r=3/5. For N=M+c (c even, small) N≡1+c (mod d). Find smallest odd d|c+1 with known r: d=11→r=6/11, d=7→4/7, d=5→3/5, d=3→2/3. Compute r_i, sum S=∑factor_i·r_i (factor=1,5). S=60/11 →p+q=71. Mod 99991=71.

We need f(N)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N. Write a=ts,b=tr,c=tu·m (m≥1, u=lcm(s,r)). Then N=t(s+r+u·m). For each base (s,r) (gcd=1) compute ratios r(m)=u·m/(s+r+u·m). For given N, find smallest ratio among all (s,r,m) where D=s+r+u·m divides N. Use M=3^K (K=2025!). For N=M, D=9 (s=1,r=2,m=3) gives ratio 2/3 → f(M)=2/3 M. For N=5M, D=15 (s=1,r=2,m=7) gives ratio 3/5 → f(5M)=3/5 5M. For N=M+c (c small), test D values from base pairs (including m>1) in order of increasing ratio (2/3,3/5,4/7,6/11,…). Compute smallest D|N, then g(c)=u·m/D (since K·u·m/D integer). Sum fractions → 60/11 → p+q=71. Pitfall: consider m>1 (D=s+r+u·m), not only m=1.

Use f(N)=r·N where r=pq/(pq+p+q) and N must be multiple of L(p,q)=D·lcm(p2,q2). For N=M (3^k) only L=9 works →r=2/3. For N=5M same r=2/3. For N=M+c (c small) N≡1+c (mod L). So L must divide c+1. Factor c+1, pick divisor L from list {25,47,97,167} giving smallest r: 16/25,30/47,64/97,110/167. Sum r’s = 2/3+2/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167 = 224414944/57101475. p+q mod 99991 = 41754.
